newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Protesters clash with police in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Protesters clash with police in Bangladesh.

text.p: Protesters clashed with police and attacked vehicles on Dhaka's streets on Thursday after the arrest of four key leaders of the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), witnesses said.
"Small groups of protesters converged at the city centre from all directions, pelted stones at baton-weilding police and damaged at least a dozen cars," one witness said.
They shouted anti-government slogans and threatened tougher action unless the arrested leaders were freed immediately.
Police drove away the protesters with batons, reporters and photographers on the scene said.
Three protesters were detained, they said.
Arrested in the pre-dawn swoop were former ministers Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, Abdul Mannan and Goyeswar Roy, and former Mayor of Dhaka Mirza Abbas.
Police also raided the house of former minister Sadek Hossain Khoka but he managed to escape, his family said.
One BNP leader told Reuters by telephone that many party stalwarts had been in hiding to escape arrest.

The raid followed BNP's call on Wednesday for a countrywide general strike on Sunday, a working day in mainly Moslem Bangladesh, in an attempt to topple the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
"We can't give them any more time. They have proved more than inefficient in running the country," BNP chief and former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia told a party rally in Dhaka.
A relative of Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, former energy minister, said: "Hundreds of police in uniform and civil dress stormed our house around 5 a.m. and just asked him to follow them."
A nephew of Abdul Mannan, former textile and civil aviation minister, added: "They produced no warrants and explained nothing."
Police said the former ministers were picked up by detectives but would not say on what charges.
Political analysts were divided on the possible impact of the arrests.
Some said they believed the "hard line" taken by Hasina's government was necessary to ensure political stability. Others said Hasina should have waited for public reaction to BNP's strike call.
Khaleda branded Hasina's government "shamelessly pro-Indian", and said it had conspired to "let the big hegemonist power enhance its influence on the small neighbour".
"We can no longer cooperate with this government or keep silent when national interests are at stake," Khaleda told cheering supporters.
Khaleda also attacked Hasina's handling of the economy.
Hasina took office last June after the Awami League defeated the BNP in general elections billed free and fair at home and abroad.
The strike is the first major challenge faced by the eight-month-old government.
